Football stadium in Bochum, Germany. It is the home ground for the VfL Bochum and has a capacity of 27,599. The stadium has a capacity of 27,599 people. The stadium was expanded between March 1976 and July 1979 and the first game was between the VfL Bochum and SG Wattenscheid 09 on 21 July 1979. Additionally, his song Bochum is sung before the kickoff of every home match of VfL Bochum, with the final line before the final chorus of the piece bearing special significance to the club. In 2016, a new naming rights deal was struck with the German housing association Vonovia, and the stadium was rebranded as Vonovia Ruhrstadion.

title: Vfl Bochum 1848 (Vonovia Ruhrstadion)
content: Vfl Bochum 1848 (Vonovia Ruhrstadion). # Vonovia Ruhrstadion. The stadium is known by traditional fans as the Ruhrstadion, and the Bochum-based stadium has been open for 112 years. From 2006 to 2016, Vfl Bochum’s stadium was called the rewirpowerSTADion and since 2016 the stadium has been called the Vonovia Ruhrstadion. With a capacity of 26,000 for Vfl Bochum’s home games, Vonovia Ruhrstadion is the 17th biggest stadium in the Bundesliga. Vonovia Ruhrstadion has hosted four Germany matches since 1922. Finally, Germany beat Ghana 6-1 in a friendly on 14 April 1993, which is the last Germany game that has been played at the Vonovia Ruhrstadion. Matchday tickets can be purchased at the stadium in the fanshop or on the Vfl Bochum 1848 website. Tickets for Vfl Bochum 1848 home games are split into Category A and Category B games. #### Be the first to leave a review of Vfl Bochum 1848 (Vonovia Ruhrstadion)!

title: Vonovia Ruhrstadion - Bochum - The Stadium Guide
content: The roots of Vonovia Ruhrstadion, previously called simply Ruhrstadion and rewirpowerStadion for sponsor reasons, go back to October 1911 when a first sports field was opened at the site of the current stadium. In 2006 the stadium changed its name to rewirpowerStadion as part of a sponsorship deal, which got changed to Vonovia Ruhrstadion in 2016 following a new deal. Vonovia Ruhrstadion is located toward the north-east of the city of Bochum, only slightly more than a kilometre away from Bochum’s city centre and a little less than two kilometres from Bochum’s main railway station. Following the Castroper Straße north by foot will get you from the centre to the stadium in 15 to 20 minutes. Tickets for VFL Bochum games can be bought online, by phone +49 18 05 95 18 48, at the Fanshop at the stadium, or at one of the other sales points, which include the Tourist Centre at the Huestraße 9 in Bochum’s city centre.
